t:
(a) Section 2002(a)(11) of the Social Security Act is amended—

        (1) 
by striking out “and” at the end of subparagraph (C);
 
        (2) 
by striking out the period at the end of subparagraph (D) and inserting in lieu thereof “; and”; and
 
        (3) 
by adding at the end thereof the following new subparagraph:


“(E) 
any expenditure for the provision of emergency shelter, for not in excess of thirty days in any six-month period, provided as a protective service to an adult in danger of physical or mental injury, neglect, maltreatment, or exploitation.”.
  
    (b) The amendments made by this section shall be effective on and after October 1, 1979.

fable.w: This section only amends the Social Security Act to add a category of expenditure (emergency shelter as a protective service for adults) and sets an effective date. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge a federal decision, and there is no rulemaking, comment period, or advisory body. The only possible temptation is that it concerns services to the public, but receiving a benefit or funded service is not participation in a federal decision.
fable.s: any expenditure for the provision of emergency shelter, for not in excess of thirty days in any six-month period, provided as a protective service to an adult in danger of physical or mental injury, neglect, maltreatment, or exploitation.

opus.w: The section adds emergency shelter, for up to thirty days in any six-month period, to the expenditures covered under Section 2002(a)(11), and sets an effective date. It does not require a comment period, rulemaking, a hearing, an advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or any right to sue. Mentioning services for vulnerable adults is about what can be funded, not about anyone taking part in a federal decision.
opus.b: I find no participation here. Someone might be tempted to read the reference to protective services for at-risk adults as involving outside parties. That reading fails because the amendment only adds a category of expenditure to the Social Security Act's funding provisions. Funding coverage is about what money can be spent on, not about outsiders taking part in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Social Security Act to define eligible expenditures for emergency shelter and sets an effective date. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from any outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making a decision. The text describes eligibility criteria for funding, not a participatory process for federal decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Section 2002(a)(11) of the Social Security Act is amended— ... (3) by adding at the end thereof the following new subparagraph: “(E) any expenditure for the provision of emergency shelter, for not in excess of thirty days in any six-month period, provided as a protective service to an adult in danger of physical or mental injury, neglect, maltreatment, or exploitation.”. (b) The amendments made by this section shall be effective on and after October 1, 1979.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the statute defines what expenditures are eligible for federal funding, it implicitly involves participation by states or providers in the decision-making process regarding how funds are used. However, the text itself only amends the definition of eligible expenses and sets an effective date. It does not mandate any consultation, public comment, advisory board, or coordination with outside parties. The decision of whether to provide shelter is made by the state/local provider, and the federal role is limited to reimbursement based on the defined criteria. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with outsiders before making a decision; rather, it sets the rules for reimbursement.
